correctness.rationale: The definition, fixed-point conditioning, parity constraints, and \(n\ge4\) denominator are explicit. Weighted involution RSK/Littlewood coefficient identity gives position-invariant one- and two-ascent counts; Burnside orbits yield A2 and A22. Substituting I(n-r,f-s)/I(n,f) simplifies to the stated exact covariance. Cubic derivative has negative discriminant, with opposing endpoint signs, giving the unique threshold. Rescaling f by \(n^{2/3}\) proves the critical limit. The embedded exact verifier exhaustively checked 48,920 involutions of sizes four to eleven and 3,743 comparisons including rational closed formulas through \(n=100\); finite tests are only supplementary.

originality.rationale: The fixed-point-free specialization and the full fixed-point-weighted descent-set enumerator are explicitly prior art (Kim 2017; Chow 2008). The narrower claimed contribution is the conditioned signed covariance across all admissible f, unique cubic threshold, and \(n^{2/3}\) critical scaling. These are absent from inspected primary statements and published-finding corpus matches. Although derivable from the classical enumerator, extracting and classifying the sign is the asserted new mathematical property; broader full-enumeration coverage is an explicit residual risk.

value.rationale: This is a natural local-correlation observable for conditioned random involutions, not an arbitrary parameter slice. A complete all-n sign classification exhibits positive-to-negative correlation under increasing prescribed fixed points at the unusual mesoscopic scale \(n^{2/3}\), invisible in fixed-positive-fraction asymptotic normality. The explicit critical profile quantifies the boundary relevant to understanding weak long-range dependence of descent statistics; the paper does not claim a downstream theorem.
